children: Abu Dhabi’s residential market is expected to witness further, measured softening in prices and rents as new supply gradually widens buyer and tenant choice, according to a Cushman & Wakefield Core report.

City-wide sales prices declined 1% quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) in the second quarter, the first decline since late 2021, but remained 22% higher year-on-year (YoY), the consultancy said in its H1 2026 Abu Dhabi Mid-Year Market Update.

New residential launches nearly doubled annually, from 7,019 units across 29 projects in the first half of 2025 to 13,073 units across 43 projects in the first half of 2026. Upcoming deliveries will remain concentrated within major master-planned communities.

Off-plan sales remained particularly strong, running at around five times secondary market volumes. City-wide average residential sales prices reached AED 16,368 ($4,456.91) per square metre (sqm) in the second quarter of 2026, up 22% YoY, but down 1% QoQ, the first quarterly dip since late 2021.

Average residential rents reached AED 945 per sqm per year in the second quarter of 2026, up 4% YoY, but down 5% QoQ. Saadiyat Island (+18%) and Al Raha Beach (+13%) led apartment growth, while villas were mixed, up 17-23% in Saadiyat and Yas Island versus a 10% decline in Al Raha Gardens.

“Abu Dhabi’s growth has largely leaned on its government-backed developers, and rather than pulling back amid regional uncertainty, they repositioned toward end-user demand and mid-prime product,” Prathyusha Gurrapu, Head of Research at Cushman & Wakefield Core, said.
Office rents rose 15% QoQ and 32% YoY to AED 2,182 per sqm per year, with prime and grade A occupancy at around 99% and city-wide office occupancy at 93%.
“With little meaningful new supply expected in the near term, conditions are likely to remain in landlords’ favour,” the report stated.

title: Abu Dhabi’s residential market to see further softening in prices, rents - report
